 Petrol prices near lowest level since March as oil prices fall 
 Tuesday, 10 November 2026 - 13:40
 The recommended price of petrol is approaching its lowest point since March, following a sharp decline in oil prices this month. Hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the war in the Middle East have contributed to the drop.
 Euro95 petrol had a recommended price of 2.442 euros per liter on Tuesday, figures from consumer platform UnitedConsumers show. It is close to the lowest price recorded since March, when the outbreak of the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz triggered a sharp increase in fuel costs. The price dipped below Tuesday's level only briefly in June, hitting 2.433 euros per liter on June 19.
 Diesel prices have also continued to decline, with the recommended price dropping to 2.569 euros per liter, its lowest point since the end of August.
 Changes in oil prices typically take some time to be reflected at petrol stations. Crude oil prices declined again on Tuesday, partly amid hopes that last week's Democratic victory in the midterm elections could pave the way for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict between the United States and Iran. The war has driven up oil prices worldwide.
 Brent crude briefly dropped below 90 dollars per barrel on Tuesday, marking its lowest level since August. The benchmark oil price, which reflects supplies from the Middle East and Europe, had stood at more than 117 dollars per barrel at the end of October.
 Despite the recent decline, fuel prices remain above pre-war levels. At the end of February, before the conflict in the Middle East began, the recommended price was 2.285 euros per liter for petrol and 2.084 euros per liter for diesel.
